clue.text: Difficult to give one's support to book

parts.note: to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone finds it hard to get behind a particular book.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers, as opposed to a paperback edition.

clue.text: Angry at pointless purchases made

indicators.note: points are compass points N, S, E and W, so each word must lose one of those letters

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about buying things that turned out to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOPPING drops its S and MADE drops its E, both compass points, leaving HOPPING MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopping mad is an informal idiom for extremely furious, as if jumping with rage.

clue.text: Suspect lied a treat and got hit back!

indicators.note: something suspect is dubious or not right, so the letters that follow are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A suspect told a great lie and was struck in return.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to strike back or take revenge after being attacked or wronged.

clue.text: Makes off with rolls of fabric

definitions.meaning: second meaning: lengths of cloth wound on a roll

explanation.surface: A thief runs away carrying bundles of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who bolts flees in haste, and bolts of cloth are long rolled lengths sold by drapers.

clue.text: Getting jam on middle of newspaper article

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits beside it in the column, joining them

parts.note: jam is a spread for bread

explanation.surface: Someone smears jam on the middle pages of a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A centre spread is a feature printed across the two facing pages in the middle of a newspaper or magazine.

clue.text: Schedule time and rearrange

parts.note: an age is a period of time

indicators.note: to rearrange is to put items in a different order, so the small word before it is shuffled

explanation.surface: An instruction to plan a time and then reorganise the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list of items to be dealt with, a programme or schedule for a meeting.

clue.text: Train worker to track safety device

parts.note: the guard is the railway official on a train
a rail is a piece of railway track

explanation.surface: A railway employee heads out to the line to fit a piece of protective equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardrail is a barrier fitted along a road edge or stairway to prevent falls or collisions.

clue.text: Record the rise of the public school

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads from bottom to top, so the word runs upwards

parts.note: Eton College, the famous English public (fee-paying) school

explanation.surface: A history recording how a particular private school became prominent.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is an expensive private boarding school; Eton is the best known.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to write it down or record it, and a note is also a written record.

clue.text: Help to take a gamble

parts.note: a bet is a wager or gamble

explanation.surface: Assistance in placing a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing, as in aiding and abetting.

clue.text: Cross-bred from sort of petal and nut

indicators.note: something bred is produced anew, so the letters that follow are made into something new
a sort of something is a variant version, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters to shuffle, the joining word dropped

explanation.surface: A hybrid plant produced from a strange flower and a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross-bred' reads as one horticultural word, but the hyphen splits it: Cross is the definition and bred signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant means sulky and bad-tempered, so cross here is the adjective for being annoyed.

clue.text: Servant let out old item of clothing

indicators.note: letters that are out are disordered, so the word before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A servant releases a cloak from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a loose sleeveless cloak, a garment chiefly of earlier centuries.

clue.text: Express trains can be educational places

parts.note: to state is to express in words
to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: Fast railway services can be educational, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Express and trains look like a railway pairing, but both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: State schools are publicly funded schools, establishments where children are taught at no charge.

clue.text: Showed a trusted doctor puts sick first

indicators.note: puts with first means one piece is placed at the front of the other
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters before it are altered

explanation.surface: A reliable physician demonstrates that he prioritises the sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like the person but is the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: To illustrate is to show or demonstrate by example, so illustrated is past tense like showed.

clue.text: Cut off supply to woman's associate

parts.note: a common woman's name, short for Diana
the possessive ending taken as written
to connect things is to associate them

explanation.surface: A company stops providing a service to a woman's business partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A utility disconnects a customer when it stops the flow of gas, power or phone service.

clue.text: Less prominent parts revealed as I undressed to change

indicators.note: the words before must change their order to produce something new

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off to get changed shows body parts usually kept hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Undersides are the lower or bottom surfaces of things, the parts least visible.

clue.text: Fine of GBP 1,000

definitions.meaning: second meaning: slang for a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A penalty of a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine reads as a penalty, but it is the adjective meaning splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand means magnificent or excellent, and a grand is informal for a thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: Obediently, I totally follow partial charge on goods

indicators.note: only part of the following word is used, so it loses its last letter
the pieces before it come after the shortened word in the answer

parts.note: duty is a tax levied on imported goods

explanation.surface: A person explains they completely accept part of an import tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something dutifully means doing it as duty requires, respectfully and compliantly.

clue.text: Circumstances surrounding the job

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the state of affairs around something
second meaning: a post or position of employment

explanation.surface: The background facts relating to a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a set of conditions in which one finds oneself, and also a formal word for a post, as in situations vacant.

clue.text: Openings for a photographer

parts.note: surface reading: job vacancies for someone who takes pictures
setter's reading: the holes in a camera lens that let light through

explanation.walkthrough: Openings suggests employment opportunities, but the photographer's openings are physical gaps in the lens.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a hole or gap, specifically the adjustable opening controlling light entering a camera.

clue.text: Cruel manoeuvre results in financial gain

indicators.note: a manoeuvre moves things about, so the word before it is reshuffled

explanation.surface: A heartless business tactic pays off in money.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or profit, especially when gained dishonourably, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Showy details are potential sources of conflict

explanation.surface: Ostentatious trimmings are what start arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashpoints are places or situations where violence or trouble is likely to erupt.

clue.text: Bird found by river and lake

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bird spotted near water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The ousel, or ouzel, is an old name for the blackbird and also the ring ouzel, a thrush.

clue.text: A bit overcome by trick

indicators.note: read as over-come, the word is turned over, which in a down clue flips it end to end

parts.note: a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly beaten by deception.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap is a trick or ruse designed to catch someone out.

clue.text: Pram designed for slope

indicators.note: something designed is newly worked out, so the word before it is put in fresh order

explanation.surface: A baby carriage built for going up and down inclines.
explanation.walkthrough: A pram is a British baby carriage or stroller.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is an inclined surface joining two levels, which suits prams and wheelchairs.

clue.text: Is it true about one's friend?

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a rumour concerning their friend is accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: Really? is an exclamation of surprised doubt, asking whether something is actually so.

clue.text: Animals lead towards source of drink

explanation.surface: Livestock are driven to a watering place.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask holding beer or wine, from which drink is drawn.

clue.text: Look fit to burst, showing animated character

indicators.note: to fit one thing to another is to attach it, so the two pieces are joined

parts.note: to eye is to look at

explanation.surface: Someone looking ready to explode reveals a cartoon persona.
explanation.walkthrough: Fit to burst sounds like an idiom for bulging, but it means attach to burst.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor is a cartoon figure who gains strength by eating spinach.

clue.text: Singles out aisles to be rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged says the preceding letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone picks out particular supermarket aisles for redesign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to set apart or separate something from others, as singling out does.
